newsitem.title: USA: NY officials vow to block Gravano profits.
newsitem.headline: NY officials vow to block Gravano profits.

text.p: Gov. George Pataki said Wednesday the state would sue to recover any profits mob turncoat Salvatore "Sammy Bull" Gravano might make on his reportedly lucrative book deal.
Profits by Gravano from such a deal would be "unconscionable," Pataki said in a statement.
Gravano confessed to 19 murders as part of his deal with federal prosecutors to testify against various organised crime figures, including reputed mob boss John Gotti.
Largely on Gravano's testimony, Gotti, the former head of the Gambino crime family, was convicted in 1992 of murder and racketeering. He is serving life without parole in a federal prison.
Gravano spent five years in prison as part of his plea deal, and he is now in hiding in the government's witness protection programme.
Pataki said he asked the state's Crime Victims Board to take steps to ensure that Gravano does not profit from any book deal.
"He should not be allowed to prey on the families of his victims a second time by telling his disgusting story, compounding their tragic loss," he said.
Two daughters of Gravano's last murder victim, reputed Gambino associate Eddie Garafalo, have filed claims with the Crime Victims Board.
New York Attorney General Dennis Vacco said the state will file suit under the so-called Son of Sam Law, which limits the ability of convicted criminals to profit from accounts of their crimes.
The law is named after David Berkowitz, the notorious serial killer who called himself "Son of Sam" and preyed upon women in New York City in the late 1970s.
Gravano has reportedly signed a six-figure book deal and and is collaborating with author Peter Maas, who wrote the bestsellers "Serpico" and "The Valachi Papers."
